role: Literature Scout + Evidence Extractor: automated science, metascience, multi-agent systems
objective: Map AI-scientist systems, hypothesis generation/ranking, evaluations and critiques, metascience (reproducibility, preregistration, systematic review / meta-analysis), calibration, multi-agent orchestration and failure modes, agent memory/RAG/knowledge graphs, recursive self-improvement.
research_question: What design choices demonstrably improve reliability of autonomous research agents, and which failure modes are documented?
context: Autonomous research lab, cycle 1 (2026-10-25). Primary target: Gemma 4 E2B internals on a 2 vCPU / 8 GiB CPU-only sandbox.
allowed_methods: OpenAlex API (works search, referenced_works for backward, filter=cites:W... for forward citations)
Semantic Scholar API (rate-limited; backoff, sparing use)
GitHub pages of code repos (read only)
evidence_requirements: Every source row must have a resolvable URL or DOI/arXiv id verified by an actual API/web call in this task. read_depth must honestly reflect what was read: full_text | partial | abstract_only | metadata_only. Claims are attributed to authors ('authors report ...'), never asserted as established truth.
budget: ≈150 tool calls; target 40-90 deduplicated relevant sources; stop earlier at saturation
acceptance_criteria: ≥8 foundational + ≥10 recent (2024-2026) primary sources; backward AND forward citation search done for ≥3 anchor papers; ≥3 critical/negative/replication works if they exist; saturation statement with evidence (last N queries yielded <10% new relevant items); explicit gap list.
stop_condition: Saturation criterion met or budget exhausted; report whichever happened.
limitations: Do not run experiments, do not download model weights, do not write outside the three deliverable files, do not fabricate bibliographic data, do not upgrade abstract-level reading to full-text claims.
